title: traffic-orchestration-operator-playbook-sketches
body:
Purpose

Quick operator playbook and sketch notes for the Rollouts console focused on traffic orchestration: canary ramps, multi-variant A/B experiments, and automated fallback policies. This is a low-fidelity working doc: brain-dump of flows, recommended microcopy, edge cases, and a prioritized backlog for UX engineering to pick up.

Scope
- Console surfaces: Release Composer, Traffic Rules editor, Live Insights panel, Fallback policy composer.
- Users: SREs, platform engineers, product managers doing staged rollouts.
- Outcomes: make staged launches predictable, observable, recoverable.

Operator journey (happy path)
1) Create release: select model version(s) and route(s). Minimal required fields: name, target route(s), start time (optional).
2) Choose rollout pattern: staircase (time-based), traffic-slices (percentage by cohort), or experiment (A/B with metric set).
3) Configure gates: success metric(s), monitoring windows, health probes, and canary evaluation rules. Default preset: latency P95, error-rate, and degradation detection.
4) Start rollout: system begins incremental traffic shifts; Live Insights shows expected vs actual and signal overlays.
5) If gate fails, automatic fallback runs: either instant rollback, step back to safe percentage, or route to fallback variant.
6) Operator decision: Accept, pause, abort, or promote to full.

Wireframe notes (sketch-level)
- Release Composer (left column): name + timeline + quick presets. Large primary CTA: Start rollout. Small link: Advanced options.
- Middle column: visual traffic staircase timeline with draggable handles for each step. Hover shows step duration, percent, and predicate. Click step to open editor drawer.
- Right column: Live Insights with compact sparklines for configured metrics, live traffic distribution donut, and current action (e.g., "rolling: step 2 of 5").
- Bottom sticky bar when rollout is active with quick actions: Pause, Abort, Promote, Run Dry-check. Bar changes color based on health: green/orange/red. Tooltip offers recommended operator next steps.

Fallback policy composer (sketch)
- Template selection: soft-fallback (step back 50%), hard-fallback (rollback to previous), degraded-response (route to smaller model), custom script (advanced).
- Conditions: threshold on metric, sustained window (N minutes), consecutive failures, region-specific triggers.
- Safety throttle: minimum time between automatic fallbacks to avoid flapping.
- Preview: simulate a failing metric and show how policy would respond and which routes would be affected.

Microcopy suggestions
- Start rollout CTA: "Start rollout — begin staged traffic shift"
- Pause tooltip: "Pauses automated stepping; existing tokens will finish"
- Abort modal: "Abort will return all traffic to prior stable variant and stop the release permanently. Promoting later will require a new rollout."
- Auto-fallback confirmation: "This policy will automatically step back traffic or rollback when thresholds are met. Recommended for unattended launches."

Edge cases and open UX questions
- Cross-region discrepancies: if region A fails but region B is healthy, should fallback be per-region by default? Proposed: yes, enable region-scoped policies but require explicit opt-in.
- Flaky signals: guard against noisy metrics by requiring sustained windows and multi-metric consensus before auto-fallback.
- Multiple simultaneous rollouts to same route: introduce soft locks with warnings and an override for emergency ops.
- Observability latency: Live Insights should show data staleness indicator and a "data freshness" timestamp; if stale beyond threshold, pause automatic decisions and surface warning.

Acceptance criteria (for MVP UX)
- Create a rollout with staircase or experiment pattern in <3 screens.
- Visual timeline with draggable steps and inline percent editing.
- Attach 2+ metrics and set evaluation windows.
- Author and attach a fallback policy from templates.
- Live Insights reflecting distribution, primary metrics, and a clear health status.
- Failure triggers automatic fallback (template) and logs an event in audit trail.

Backlog (prioritized)
- RI-4001: timeline step-drag UX + keyboard input for percent (P0)
- RI-4002: fallback template builder + preview simulation modal (P0)
- RI-4003: per-region policy scoping UI and default recommendation (P1)
- RI-4010: Live Insights staleness indicator and telemetry hook (P1)
- RI-4022: experiment analysis panel with cohort breakdown and significance flags (P2)
- RI-4030: operator quickplaybook modal (one-click runbook for common failures) (P2)

Telemetry and integration notes
- Events to emit: rollout.created, rollout.step_changed, rollout.paused, rollout.fallback_triggered (include policy id), rollout.aborted, rollout.promoted.
- Include sample payload fields in implementation doc: rollout_id, step_index, percent, metric_snapshot, region, operator_id, decision_reason.
- Link to incident playbooks in runbook registry when fallback triggers.

Accessibility and localization
- All color-coded health indicators must have text labels and icons.
- Tooltips and modals support keyboard navigation and ARIA labels.
- Copy strings should be externalized for translation.

Notes to engineering and SRE reviewers
- Prefer idempotent operations for step updates (PATCH semantics).
- Rate-limit automatic fallback attempts to prevent oscillation.
- Add a safety window config at rollout creation (default: 5m) to prevent immediate rollback for transient spikes.

Next steps
- UX team: convert sketches in this doc to low-fi Figma frames. Owner: Marina. Target: 2025-03-10.
- PM: scope telemetry contract with infra and SRE. Owner: Daniel. Target: 2025-03-05.
- Backend: spike on simulation preview for fallback (estimate 3d). Owner: Jonas. Target: 2025-03-09.

Links and references
- Related console flows: CONFLUENCE-ROLL-9876 (staged rollout guidelines)
- Existing PR with rollout event schema: github.com/redwood-inference/console#PR-412
- Slack thread: #platform-release-orchestration (see pinned message)

Scratchpad (quick UX scribbles)
- Consider tiny animation when a step completes to confirm action.
- Use a compact color palette to avoid overwhelming Live Insights.
- Small confirmation delay for Abort to reduce accidental clicks (3s undo).

Unresolved
- Exact default metrics for canary eval (latency P95 + error-rate seems ok but need product signoff).
- Rollout locking behavior for testers vs production users: need policy decision.

If you iterate on this, try to keep the compositional pattern: left composer, center timeline, right live insights. Keep fallback policies templated for common operators first, then expose advanced scripting to power users.
